Finding.Text: The tool's git() helper runs git without -c core.quotepath=false and the path read-back parses "git show --pretty=format: --name-only HEAD" line-wise, while the kernel's own git helpers (src/git.ts and src/upgrade/kernel-source.ts) disable quotepath and use -z for path lists. Under git's default core.quotepath=true a supplied path containing non-ASCII characters, a double quote or a backslash is printed quoted with octal escapes; normalisePath converts the escape backslashes to slashes, so the committed-path comparison mismatches and the tool exits 1 with "committed path set differs" after creating a correct commit. The failure is reported and the commit stays visible, but a valid owned path is falsely refused and the next handoff stops on a spurious mismatch. Align the git calls with src/git.ts: pass -c core.quotepath=false and read the name list with -z. Carried forward unchanged: the source tree is identical to review-1's candidate, so the defect persists at end revision 99131735de; non-blocking, open.
